mitigation_mechanism: Zaï and tassa pits increase infiltration and the water retention capacity of the soil, so crops suffer less from drought spells at the onset of and during the rainy season [ev_soil_water_retention_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1]. In rainfall-deficit periods zaï allowed cereals to be grown on degraded crusted soils in Burkina Faso, gave sorghum in a low-rainfall year where untreated land yielded nothing, and only tassa fields produced a harvest in the 1990 drought in Niger [ev_crop_yield_roose93_3, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_6_s]. In Zimbabwe first-year planting-basin farmers obtained 1520 kg of maize per hectare against 368 kg on conventional plots in the 2006/07 season, which the source calls a drought year [ev_crop_yield_mazv09_1]. mitigation_mechanism: Runoff-fed storage carries water into dry periods: pond water used as supplemental irrigation reduces crop-loss risk in irregular years in semi-arid Brazil, cisterns catching runoff on China's Loess Plateau are credited with mitigating frequent drought, and a review of small reservoirs counts improved drought resilience among their cited benefits [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_drought_hazard_saru19_1]. WOCAT compilers for ponds and check dams in Cambodia, India, Ethiopia and Somalia rate drought impacts as reduced, the Cambodian sheet noting the pond provides enough water even during drought and the Somali sheet crediting improved soil moisture retention and infiltration [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2844_2017_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_5210_2019_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_drought_impacts]. Stored water bridges dry spells: a water-harvesting review cites supplemental irrigation of 50–200 mm bridging critical dry spells and stabilising yields, and rainwater management is cited as letting producers avoid total crop loss in critical drought periods [ev_yield_stability_rock10_1, ev_crop_yield_silv26_2]. Indian farmers reported a 6% chance of rainy-season crop failure from aberrant rains with a farm pond against 20% in the same crop–tree–livestock system without a pond [ev_yield_stability_pals23_1]. mitigation_mechanism: Terraces, stone bunds and infiltration trenches slow and spread runoff on slopes: terraces lowered mean runoff and flood peaks on small mountain plots, stone bunds lower peak discharges at the foot of the slope, trenches significantly reduced plot runoff across the reviewed studies, and a combined treatment in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment reduced flood runoff volume, clipped peaks and lengthened flood duration [ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_1, ev_runoff_reduction_locat20_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s]. A check-dam review cites check dams mitigating flooding and significantly reducing peak flow in Iran and check-dam sequences proving effective against strong floods in Italian torrents, and small hill dams in Morocco are credited with damping damage during the serious 2002-2003 floods [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2, ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1]. Spate and diversion structures in Yemen are reported to control floods, users of small reservoirs in Ghana perceive flood limitation as a benefit, compacted hill terraces in Uttarakhand, India are credited with limiting flood and landslide damage, and WOCAT compilers across sheets from Ethiopia, Kenya, Tunisia, Somalia, Uzbekistan and other countries rate flooding as reduced, the Kenyan compiler noting a dam or series of dams buffers downstream flooding [ev_flood_hazard_yem12_4, ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1, ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1537_2012_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_downstream_flooding].
caveats: The same check-dam review finds a minimal effect against extreme floods, especially where structures were ill-designed and not maintained [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_3]. Diversion structures can work the other way: diversion banquettes in Niger raised peak discharges, runoff-diversion systems accelerate concentration time, and larger sand dams increase flooding risk [ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_3, ev_flood_hazard_ritc21_1]. Catchment-level terrace evidence is scarce, most measured results are at plot or hillslope scale, the Tunisian catchment result bundles rangeland closure and gully stone-filling with the bunds, and the Italian check-dam cases are mountain torrent control in a high-income setting rather than farm water harvesting [ev_flood_hazard_willem21_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2]. Most units are WOCAT compiler ratings: the Philippine sheet rates flood impacts as worse, the Indian farm-pond sheet rates downstream flooding as unchanged, the Zambian compiler says the benefit holds only at large scale, and a Somali sheet scores downstream flooding in the worsening direction although its comment says flooding was reduced [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1021_2011_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1474_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1139_2013_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_downstream_flooding].

justification.mechanism: Terraces, stone bunds and infiltration trenches slow and spread runoff on slopes: terraces lowered mean runoff and flood peaks on small mountain plots, stone bunds lower peak discharges at the foot of the slope, trenches significantly reduced plot runoff across the reviewed studies, and a combined treatment in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment reduced flood runoff volume, clipped peaks and lengthened flood duration [ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_1, ev_runoff_reduction_locat20_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s]. Spate and diversion structures in Yemen are reported to control floods, users of small reservoirs in Ghana perceive flood limitation as a benefit, compacted hill terraces in Uttarakhand, India are credited with limiting flood and landslide damage, and WOCAT compilers across sheets from Ethiopia, Kenya, Tunisia, Somalia, Uzbekistan and other countries rate flooding as reduced, the Kenyan compiler noting a dam or series of dams buffers downstream flooding [ev_flood_hazard_yem12_4, ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1, ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1537_2012_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_downstream_flooding].

Diversion structures can work the other way: diversion banquettes in Niger raised peak discharges, runoff-diversion systems accelerate concentration time, and larger sand dams increase flooding risk [ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_3, ev_flood_hazard_ritc21_1]. A check-dam review cites check dams mitigating flooding and significantly reducing peak flow in Iran and check-dam sequences proving effective against strong floods in Italian torrents, and small hill dams in Morocco are credited with damping damage during the serious 2002-2003 floods [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2, ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1]. WOCAT compilers for sheets in China, Tunisia, Nicaragua and Syria also rate downstream flooding as reduced [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1455_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1400_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1719_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1005_2011_downstream_flooding].
justification.conditionality: The same check-dam review finds a minimal effect against extreme floods, especially where structures were ill-designed and not maintained [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_3]. Size can reverse the effect: larger sand dams increase the risk of flooding, erosion and seepage [ev_flood_hazard_ritc21_1]. The Indian farm-pond sheet rates downstream flooding as unchanged and a Somali sheet scores downstream flooding in the worsening direction although its comment says flooding was reduced [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1474_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_downstream_flooding]. The only peak-flow reduction is a secondary citation in a review, the Italian cases are mountain torrent control in a high-income setting, the Ghana finding is user perception and the rest are compiler ratings or institutional assertions [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2, ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1].

mitigation_mechanism: Terraces and contour stone bunds slow and spread runoff on slopes: terraces lowered mean runoff and flood peaks on small mountain plots, stone bunds lower hillslope peak discharges and in high-rainfall years protect land from rapid flow in heavy rain, and a combined treatment in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment reduced flood runoff volume, clipped peaks and lengthened flood duration [ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_1, ev_erosion_hazard_zoug14_2, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s]. Compacted hill terraces with retention walls in Uttarakhand, India are credited with mitigating flood and landslide impact, and WOCAT compilers for terraces and stone lines in Rwanda, China, Tunisia, Uzbekistan and other countries rate flooding as reduced, the Tunisian compiler noting stone lines and walls reduce peak flows during heavy rainfall [ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1553_2012_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1522_2010_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_flood_impacts].
caveats: Diversion banquettes and ditches, filed in this family, do the opposite: in Niger they raised peak discharges, and runoff-diversion systems accelerate concentration time with serious gullying risk if the dikes break [ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_3]. Catchment-level peak-flow evidence for terraces is scarce, the Tunisian result bundles rangeland closure and gully stone-filling with the bunds, the Uttarakhand claim is a Bank self-report, and most units are WOCAT compiler ratings [ev_flood_hazard_willem21_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s, ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7].

mitigation_mechanism: Practices that hold water in the field can backfire in wet conditions: stone bunds can waterlog parts of the field in wet years, millet behind stone bunds can suffer waterlogging when monthly rainfall exceeds 200 mm, and in the humid Sudanian zone of Cameroon sorghum in zaï pits yielded less than on flat-cultivated fields [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_crop_yield_roose93_4]. WOCAT compilers for pits and stone lines in Niger, conservation tillage in Kenya and the Philippines also rate drainage of excess water as worse, while compilers for terraces, check dams, water-spreading weirs and other works in Peru, Nepal, India, Yemen, Ethiopia, Cabo Verde and Jordan rate it as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1100_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_940_2010_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1506_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1493_2011_excess_water_drainage]. A conservation agriculture meta-analysis adds that 92% of the data show mulch cover in high-rainfall areas lowering maize yields through waterlogging [ev_crop_yield_rusin11_3].
caveats: The pool is split: the literature units that show harm are tied to wet years or high-rainfall zones and give no magnitude or share of field affected, while more of the units, all WOCAT practitioner ratings, report better drainage; the Chinese check-dam and Indian farm-pond sheets rate it unchanged [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1455_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1474_2011_excess_water_drainage]. The Burkina Faso statements are cited rather than measured, and the Cameroon observation is unpublished work cited by the authors [ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_crop_yield_roose93_4]. The meta-analysis figure is a share of observations, not an effect size [ev_crop_yield_rusin11_3].

mitigation_mechanism: Intense runoff overwhelms or breaks structures: floods washed away scores of small dams in northern Ghana, 37.9% of boulder-faced log check dams in Ethiopia failed after a high-magnitude runoff event, check-dam failure releases stored sediment, large floods could wash out traditional spate diversions in Yemen, banquettes lack capacity for erosive rains and overflow, and torrential rain collapses terrace walls or carries small terraces away in mass movements [ev_flood_damage_veno12_1, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_2, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_1, ev_flood_hazard_yem12_3, ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_2, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_5]. A check-dam review cites structural failure from the impact of large boulders in extreme floods, and grassed earth gully check dams in Morocco are described as fragile during major floods and needing frequent winter maintenance [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1_av, ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1_av]. WOCAT compilers judge jessour in Tunisia, zaï pits, bunds and trenches in Niger, the Vallerani system in Burkina Faso, check dam ponds in Ethiopia, radical terraces in Rwanda, gully-plugging check dams in Nepal and ripper tillage in Zambia not to cope well with river or flash floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1013_2011_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1616_2014_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1528_2012_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1547_2012_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1493_2011_general_river_flood].
caveats: Other compilers judge sand dams in Kenya, check dams in Tunisia, China and India, and spate or water-spreading systems in Eritrea and Sudan to cope well, those for marab and Vallerani systems in Jordan and a masonry check dam in Ethiopia to cope very well, and those for weirs in Ethiopia and works in Somalia to cope moderately [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1537_2012_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_5770_2020_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_6716_2023_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_7777_2026_flash_flood]; these are practitioner judgements from technology sheets, and for field-level practices (pits, bunds, tillage) a not-well rating describes exposure of fields to floodwater rather than damage to a structure. Literature failures are tied to maintenance and design: rarely maintained diversion systems generally fail after 4 to 10 years, terrace collapse is linked to abandonment, the Rwandan mass movement happened on terraces without trees, and the Moroccan earth check dams need frequent upkeep [ev_flood_hazard_roose94_2, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_5, ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1_av]. The boulder-impact and sediment-release statements are secondary citations or come from a USA study, and the Yemen statement refers to diversions before project improvements [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1_av, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_1, ev_flood_hazard_yem12_3].

mitigation_mechanism: Reservoirs, tanks and dams trap the sediment that runoff carries, so storage fills and function declines: Tigray dams with a 30-year design life were set to run their cycle in 4.4 to 5.7 years, eight of ten Zambian reservoirs lost storage to siltation, 31 percent of earthen dams in Haryana silted up within five years, Moroccan gabions had nearly lost their original function, and small hill dams in Morocco lose 0.5 to 1% of capacity each year to catchment erosion [ev_asset_siltation_saru19_1, ev_asset_siltation_saru19_4, ev_erosion_hazard_iegind11_12, ev_erosion_hazard_iegmar09_2, ev_sediment_retention_roos10_1_av]. Loose-rock check dams on semi-arid rangeland watersheds in the USA were filled to more than 80% of capacity within four years, and a review notes the sediment-control effect of check dams diminishes as they fill and becomes marginal a few years to a few decades after installation [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1_av, ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1_av]. Sedimentation is described as perhaps the primary reason for sand dam failure, and tanks desilted in an Indian programme need desilting again within its lifetime [ev_asset_failure_ritc21_3, ev_asset_siltation_verm19_1]. On Ethiopian highland bunds, a filled drainage ditch quickly lowers sediment-trapping efficiency and adds pressure that can lead to structural failure [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1_av].
caveats: Severity varies: a Kenyan sand-dam assessment estimates siltation cut storage by 10-25% and judges it neither an inherent limitation nor the main reason dams go unused [ev_asset_siltation_neuf17_1]. Most units are review citations or narrative observations without a common metric, the only directly measured fill rate comes from a high-income rangeland study, and losses depend on upkeep, as the Moroccan structures failed where no maintenance system had been put in place and small hill dams were forgotten once built [ev_asset_siltation_saru19_2, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1_av, ev_erosion_hazard_iegmar09_2, ev_sediment_retention_roos10_1_av].

Sedimentation is described as perhaps the primary reason for sand dam failure, and tanks desilted in an Indian programme need desilting again within its lifetime [ev_asset_failure_ritc21_3, ev_asset_siltation_verm19_1].
